extracted.intended_audience: journalists, local news leaders, researchers, policymakers, and the informed public
extracted.subtask_short: assessing public trust in local news
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing research findings on how the public evaluates and trusts local news organizations, including dimensions that increase or erode trust and the trade-offs between local coverage and political reporting. Useful for newsrooms, researchers, and policymakers designing or assessing local journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance of democratic roles and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Americans mostly believe local news media are doing a good job performing many of their democratic roles and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of these roles include keeping residents informed of significant local issues, holding political and civic leaders accountable, and fostering a sense of community among readers and viewers. Evaluation should consider how well a newsroom fulfills these democratic functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of important local issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Americans assess local coverage of most important local issues positively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether local outlets adequately identify and report on the 'most important local issues' as perceived by residents; positive assessments here are linked to higher trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with local community political leanings
rubrics_metrics.description: People generally see local media as in step with, rather than at odds with, the political leanings of their local community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure perceived ideological alignment between coverage and the community; alignment appears to support trust, while perceived mismatch can reduce it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevancy is a key trust dimension for local news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether content is relevant to residents' daily lives and local concerns. Greater perceived relevancy correlates with stronger trust ratings compared with national outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency is a named trust dimension for local media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider practices such as openness about sourcing, corrections, and newsroom processes; higher transparency is associated with stronger trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy / Getting the facts right
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting the facts right is a central dimension of trust; the partisan gap is especially wide on this dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess factual accuracy and clarity of reporting. The report notes Democrats are more likely than Republicans to trust local news on 'getting the facts right,' indicating accuracy perceptions strongly affect overall trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived bias (and perceived directional shift)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perceptions about whether local news has become more biased — and in what direction — strongly affect trust. While 51% do not perceive increased bias, those who do are more likely to see a shift toward liberal views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure both the presence of perceived bias and its ideological direction; the report finds that Americans who perceive a shift in bias are about half as likely to trust local news as those who do not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partisanship as an evaluative lens
rubrics_metrics.description: Partisanship is becoming a powerful lens through which people evaluate both local and national news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for respondents' partisan identities when interpreting trust measurements; partisan affiliation shapes assessments across trust dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of political/national coverage versus local content
rubrics_metrics.description: The more local news wades into coverage of national issues and aggressive social/political reporting, the more vulnerable it may be to accusations of bias and loss of community trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the balance between local-focused reporting and national/political stories. The report suggests increasing political aggression can polarize audiences and erode trust, while maintaining local focus can help preserve it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion of nonlocal versus local stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence suggests local news sources are increasingly relying on nonlocal news stories, though the public hasn’t widely noted such a shift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate newsroom content mix (local vs nonlocal); to maintain trust advantage, findings suggest increasing focus on local content is beneficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association with nonpartisan topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Local news may have built a trust advantage by being associated with reporting largely nonpartisan topics like local business development, crime, cultural events, the weather and sports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track coverage of nonpartisan beats (business, crime, culture, weather, sports) as these topics are linked to a trust advantage relative to national outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'trust advantage' relative to national media
rubrics_metrics.description: The local trust advantage appears to be more a sign of skepticism toward national media than of enthusiasm toward local news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When benchmarking trust, consider whether higher local trust scores reflect positive evaluations of local outlets or negative perceptions of national media; interpretation affects strategy and measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic mandate versus editorial risk trade-off
rubrics_metrics.description: Local news faces a dilemma: covering social and political issues is part of its mandate to help democracy flourish, but such coverage risks polarizing audiences and eroding trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance normative obligations (informing the public, accountability) with potential trust costs; decisions to pursue more aggressive political reporting should weigh democratic responsibility against possible community trust erosion.
